P01_NARROW_JOB_BRIDGE_FOUND.headline: Your hero names change. The job keeps coming back.
P01_NARROW_JOB_BRIDGE_FOUND.subheadline: Most of your regular picks return to the same few ways of starting and shaping fights.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The pool is broader by name than by function. {hero_name} is a reviewed bridge because it keeps a familiar anchor while adding a job your pool barely covers.

fallback.title: The shape is still useful
fallback.body: Your established pool has a clear functional center, even when no single expansion is the right answer.

P01_NARROW_JOB_NO_BRIDGE.headline: Your pool keeps solving Dota the same way.
P01_NARROW_JOB_NO_BRIDGE.subheadline: The repeated job is clear. A new hero recommendation is not trustworthy enough yet.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The gap is real, but a random hero would only make the card look complete. The match history, inconveniently, has standards.

fallback.title: Practice the missing job first
fallback.body: Use the uncovered function as a draft question before adding another hero to the pool.

P02_CLEAR_RELIABILITY_LADDER.headline: Your pool has a clear pecking order.
P02_CLEAR_RELIABILITY_LADDER.subheadline: A few heroes reliably carry the load; the rest are still earning that trust.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The order is stable enough to separate anchors from development picks. Practice can follow the ladder instead of treating every hero as equally ready.

fallback.title: Keep one anchor in the draft
fallback.body: Develop one lower rung at a time while preserving a hero whose results already travel.

P02_GRADUAL_RELIABILITY_LADDER.headline: Some heroes are steadier, but there is no cliff.
P02_GRADUAL_RELIABILITY_LADDER.subheadline: Reliability changes gradually across the pool rather than splitting into obvious anchors and projects.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: Use the order as a soft practice queue, not a verdict. The differences are real enough to guide attention, not large enough to exile anyone.

fallback.title: Work down the list
fallback.body: Pick one nearby hero and name the extra demand before you queue it.

P02_DEVELOPMENT_DEMAND_UNRESOLVED.headline: Your anchors are clearer than the learning problem.
P02_DEVELOPMENT_DEMAND_UNRESOLVED.subheadline: We can see which heroes hold up, but not which demand explains the developing side.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The reliability order is useful. The reason behind it needs better evidence, so the report stops before inventing a lesson.

fallback.title: Review the first hard decision
fallback.body: On the next developing pick, note the first moment when the hero asks for a decision your anchor does not.

P03_DEMAND_HYPOTHESIS.headline: Your fight presence travels. One hero demand may not.
P03_DEMAND_HYPOTHESIS.subheadline: You still show up off-pool, while the result slips and one learning demand stands out as the best lead.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The result difference is observed. The demand is a bounded hypothesis for practice, not a proven cause.

fallback.title: Test the demand
fallback.body: Use one off-pool game to watch the named demand instead of trying to fix the whole hero at once.

P03_DIRECT_DIFFERENCE_ONLY.headline: You still show up. The results stop travelling with you.
P03_DIRECT_DIFFERENCE_ONLY.subheadline: The off-pool group keeps similar involvement but loses ground on a directly observed match signal.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The difference is clear enough to name, but the cause is not. That makes it a review target, not a diagnosis.

fallback.title: Review the split
fallback.body: Compare one familiar and one off-pool match at the first point where the measured signal separates.

P03_EXPLANATION_UNRESOLVED.headline: The transfer gap is real. Its source is not clear yet.
P03_EXPLANATION_UNRESOLVED.subheadline: Your familiar and off-pool results separate, but the available summary cannot explain why.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: We would rather leave the cause blank than turn a nearby statistic into a story it did not earn.

fallback.title: Keep the question useful
fallback.body: Review entry, hold, and re-entry in one off-pool match and look for the first unfamiliar decision.

P04_GAP_WITH_BRIDGE.headline: Small pool. One useful gap.
P04_GAP_WITH_BRIDGE.subheadline: Your core covers several jobs, and {hero_name} adds the thinnest missing answer without changing everything else.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The recommendation solves the displayed coverage gap and preserves a familiar function or role anchor. It is an adjacent move, not a similarity contest.

fallback.title: The bridge is optional
fallback.body: Your current pool is already versatile. Add the hero only when the missing job matters to the draft.

P04_GAP_NO_BRIDGE.headline: Small pool. A real gap. No forced recommendation.
P04_GAP_NO_BRIDGE.subheadline: The toolkit has a thin spot, but no reviewed hero fits the role and learning distance well enough.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The gap remains useful draft information. We do not need to dress a weak candidate in confidence it did not earn.

fallback.title: Practice the function
fallback.body: Borrow the missing job in a low-stakes game or with a familiar role before expanding the permanent pool.

P04_NO_MEANINGFUL_GAP.headline: Your compact pool already covers the important jobs.
P04_NO_MEANINGFUL_GAP.subheadline: No function is thin enough to justify adding a hero just for coverage.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: Versatility is coming from functional range, not hero count. The hero browser may survive without another administrative addition.

fallback.title: Deepen instead of widening
fallback.body: Choose the existing hero whose useful job appears least often and practice making that contribution more repeatable.

P05_CONCENTRATED_FLEX_WINDOW.headline: Your flexibility has a proven window.
P05_CONCENTRATED_FLEX_WINDOW.subheadline: Several heroes and jobs repeated together during one supported stretch of matches.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: This is not a week of one-off picks. The range held together long enough to show which anchors make experimentation work.

fallback.title: Protect the anchors
fallback.body: Keep the reliable heroes warm so the wider pool has something stable to rotate around.

P05_DISTRIBUTED_FLEXIBILITY.headline: Your range is real, just spread out.
P05_DISTRIBUTED_FLEXIBILITY.subheadline: Different heroes and jobs recur across the history without one clean flex window.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The pool can change shape, but the change is gradual rather than concentrated in one chapter.

fallback.title: Keep a smaller active bench
fallback.body: Rotate a few current options around one reliable anchor instead of keeping the whole roster match-ready.

P06_HERO_CONTEXT.headline: Your rebound has a hero-shaped anchor.
P06_HERO_CONTEXT.subheadline: After a loss, your strongest next-game improvement repeats most clearly on one familiar hero.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The hero marks the cleanest observed context. It does not prove the pick causes the rebound or explain what happened in your head.

fallback.title: Simplify the next draft
fallback.body: Use the familiar hero when you want one controllable post-loss decision.

P06_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.headline: Your rebound starts with a familiar job.
P06_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.subheadline: After a loss, the next game improves most reliably when you return to one kind of contribution.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The repeatable part is the job, not a single hero. Several picks can provide the same useful anchor.

fallback.title: Return to the job
fallback.body: Choose a hero that performs the familiar function without adding a new learning problem.

P06_OVERALL_CONTEXT.headline: Your next game tends to be stronger.
P06_OVERALL_CONTEXT.subheadline: The rebound survives overall, but no hero or job explains it reliably.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The transition is worth showing. The narrower story is not, so the report leaves motive and mechanism alone.

fallback.title: Repeat what is controllable
fallback.body: Keep the next draft simple and review what changed only after the match.

P07_HERO_CONTEXT.headline: The post-loss slide clusters around one hero context.
P07_HERO_CONTEXT.subheadline: Your next-game drop is strongest when one familiar pick carries the transition.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The hero localizes the pattern; it does not become the villain. Draft, matchup, and session context can still matter.

fallback.title: Change one transition
fallback.body: After a loss, pause before returning to this pick or change one part of the plan around it.

P07_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.headline: The post-loss slide is shaped by the job.
P07_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.subheadline: Your next-game drop repeats most clearly when you return to one kind of contribution.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The function is the useful boundary. The result does not justify blaming every hero that can perform it.

fallback.title: Change the job once
fallback.body: Use a stable alternative contribution in the next game and keep the rest of the draft familiar.

P07_OVERALL_CONTEXT.headline: Your next game tends to lose ground.
P07_OVERALL_CONTEXT.subheadline: The slide is broad enough to repeat, but no narrower context is stable enough to name.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The transition is observable. Tilt, confidence, and intent are not.

fallback.title: Interrupt the queue once
fallback.body: Pause, return to a stable pick, or simplify the first game plan. One change is enough.

P08_HERO_CONTEXT.headline: One hero gives you presence without the usual death bill.
P08_HERO_CONTEXT.subheadline: Your cleanest high-involvement, low-exposure context belongs to a specific pick.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: This hero repeatedly lets you contribute while staying available for the next move. The enemy sees you often. Catching you appears to be the administrative problem.

fallback.title: Preserve the useful shape
fallback.body: Keep the positioning and commitment pattern that makes this hero's presence sustainable.

P08_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.headline: One job keeps your presence efficient.
P08_FUNCTION_CONTEXT.subheadline: High involvement and lower death exposure repeat most clearly across a shared function.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The useful part travels across heroes because the contribution itself asks for less costly exposure.

fallback.title: Draft for the job
fallback.body: Choose another reviewed hero that preserves the same function and commitment level.

P08_OVERALL_CONTEXT.headline: You stay involved without paying the full cost.
P08_OVERALL_CONTEXT.subheadline: The relationship holds overall, though no hero or job owns it strongly enough.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The broad pattern is earned. A narrower explanation would be decoration.

fallback.title: Preserve the broad habit
fallback.body: Review the fights where you contribute and still remain available for the next objective.

P09_JOB_SHAPED.headline: Going first carries most of your death cost.
P09_JOB_SHAPED.subheadline: High involvement and high exposure cluster around the job that starts the fight.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The cost is functional rather than universal. Initiation asks you to enter danger before everyone else; Dota has implemented an entry fee.

fallback.title: Check for follow-up
fallback.body: Before committing, verify that teammates can reach the target or that your kit has a second move.

P09_HERO_SPECIFIC.headline: One hero carries most of the presence tax.
P09_HERO_SPECIFIC.subheadline: The death cost concentrates on a specific pick instead of following the whole pool.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The hero is the best review target, not proof that every death was wrong or that the pick is bad.

fallback.title: Review the expensive entries
fallback.body: Separate deaths that buy fights, saves, or objectives from entries with no reachable follow-up.

P09_CROSS_CONTEXT.headline: Your presence tax follows you across contexts.
P09_CROSS_CONTEXT.subheadline: High involvement and high exposure remain linked across several heroes and jobs.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The cost is broader than one pick. Summary history cannot tell which deaths bought value, so replay review is the next honest step.

fallback.title: Review the decision before entry
fallback.body: Look for target reach, teammate distance, and a second move before the highest-cost commitments.

P09_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.headline: The death cost is visible. Its source is not.
P09_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.subheadline: High involvement and exposure move together, but the available subgroups do not localize the pattern.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The report can show the bill without pretending to know who placed the order.

fallback.title: Use replay evidence
fallback.body: Review a small set of high-exposure fights and classify what each death actually bought.

P10_STABLE_BREAKPOINT.headline: Your results usually start slipping at {session_game_label}.
P10_STABLE_BREAKPOINT.subheadline: The earlier games stay near your usual level; the later ones move down often enough to mark a repeatable checkpoint.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The breakpoint is a warning light, not a curfew. It gives you a moment to choose deliberately before the queue button makes another perfectly functional appearance.

fallback.title: Use the checkpoint
fallback.body: Pause, return to a familiar role, or stop—pick one deliberate response.

P10_GRADUAL_FADE.headline: Your results fade gradually across longer sessions.
P10_GRADUAL_FADE.subheadline: There is no single drop; each later game gives up a little more ground.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The shape is useful even without a magic game number. Treat the session as a slope, not a trapdoor.

fallback.title: Add an earlier checkpoint
fallback.body: Check whether another game still sounds useful before the curve has already done the deciding.

P10_BREAKPOINT_UNRESOLVED.headline: Later games look weaker, but the turning point moves.
P10_BREAKPOINT_UNRESOLVED.subheadline: The session trend qualifies without one stable game where the fade begins.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The broad pattern is worth showing. A precise breakpoint would be false accuracy.

fallback.title: Use a personal checkpoint
fallback.body: Choose a simple review moment—after two losses or before Game 4—and decide deliberately.

P11_STABLE_BREAKPOINT.headline: Your session usually turns up at {session_game_label}.
P11_STABLE_BREAKPOINT.subheadline: The later games rise above your usual level often enough to mark a repeatable lift point.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: You tend to warm into the session. The number is a planning clue, not a requirement for ceremonial early-game sacrifices.

fallback.title: Front-load familiarity
fallback.body: Use a stable role and hero before the lift, then move experimentation later.

P11_GRADUAL_RISE.headline: You warm into sessions one game at a time.
P11_GRADUAL_RISE.subheadline: Results improve gradually rather than jumping at one clean breakpoint.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The lift is a slope. Early familiarity gives the later games more room for complexity.

fallback.title: Start simple
fallback.body: Open with a familiar role, hero, and plan; add novelty only after the session settles.

P11_BREAKPOINT_UNRESOLVED.headline: Later games improve, but the lift point moves.
P11_BREAKPOINT_UNRESOLVED.subheadline: The upward session pattern repeats without one stable game where it begins.

interpretation.title: What this means
interpretation.body: The warming pattern is earned. A precise game number is not.

fallback.title: Keep the opening familiar
fallback.body: Use the first games to enter the session cleanly and delay the harder experiment.

HR_DOUBLE_DOWN.title: Deepen the answer you already trust
HR_DOUBLE_DOWN.body: Use {hero_name} when you want the familiar job with stronger role fit and fewer new demands.

HR_ADJACENT_MOVE_ADD_FUNCTION.title: Add one new answer, not a new identity
HR_ADJACENT_MOVE_ADD_FUNCTION.body: Try {hero_name}: it keeps a familiar anchor and adds the function your pool is missing.

HR_SPECIALIST.title: Add a deliberate specialist
HR_SPECIALIST.body: Try {hero_name} when the draft rewards its narrow answer. The learning jump is part of the recommendation, not fine print.

HR_PRACTICE_FALLBACK.title: Practice the gap before adding a hero
HR_PRACTICE_FALLBACK.body: Use the displayed function or demand as the next-match question. We do not have a hero recommendation we trust enough yet.

HR_CHANGE_ANGLE.title: Change one contribution
HR_CHANGE_ANGLE.body: Use {hero_name} to approach the same role from a different angle, with the new demands named before you queue.

HR_PRACTICE_TRANSFER_DEMAND.title: Practice the demand that stops travelling
HR_PRACTICE_TRANSFER_DEMAND.body: Focus the next off-pool game on the named demand. Keep the result difference as evidence, not a verdict.

HR_FILL_GAP_ADD_FUNCTION.title: Fill the exact gap
HR_FILL_GAP_ADD_FUNCTION.body: Try {hero_name} when the draft needs {function_name}; it preserves {familiar_anchor} while adding the missing answer.

HR_PROTECT_RELIABLE_ANCHOR.title: Keep the anchors warm
HR_PROTECT_RELIABLE_ANCHOR.body: Protect the heroes that make your range repeatable instead of keeping the entire pool equally ready.

HR_REPEAT_POST_LOSS_ANCHOR.title: Simplify the first post-loss decision
HR_REPEAT_POST_LOSS_ANCHOR.body: Return to the strongest supported hero or job anchor and let the rest of the draft stay ordinary.

HR_CHANGE_ONE_TRANSITION.title: Change one transition
HR_CHANGE_ONE_TRANSITION.body: Pause the queue, return to a stable pick, or simplify the first plan. One controllable change is enough.

HR_PRESERVE_LOW_COST_PRESENCE.title: Preserve the useful shape
HR_PRESERVE_LOW_COST_PRESENCE.body: Keep the job, positioning, or commitment pattern that gives you involvement without the same death cost.

HR_INVESTIGATE_PRESENCE_COST.title: Separate useful cost from exposure
HR_INVESTIGATE_PRESENCE_COST.body: Use the strongest context to find which deaths buy fights, saves, or objectives—and which buy paperwork.

HR_CHECKPOINT_AT_BREAKPOINT.title: Use the breakpoint as a checkpoint
HR_CHECKPOINT_AT_BREAKPOINT.body: At {session_game_label}, choose a pause, familiar role, or stop before autopilot chooses for you.

HR_FRONTLOAD_FAMILIARITY.title: Front-load familiarity
HR_FRONTLOAD_FAMILIARITY.body: Start with a reliable role, hero, and plan; move the harder experiment after the session has warmed up.
